title: Failure Saga Explorer and Query Playbook for Multi-Layer Error Attribution
creator: Asha Patel
description: Summary: Build a cross-layer interactive dashboard and a query playbook (Failure Saga Explorer) that unifies traces, metric spikes, and log excerpts to categorize failures into canonical types: client/network timeouts, gateway overload, runtime preemption, model rejections/garbage responses, and HTTP/gRPC-coded errors. Goals: 1) Provide engineers and oncall with a single-pane failure investigation view that surfaces probable cause and actionable next steps. 2) Standardize failure taxonomy and a reproducible query/playbook that converts telemetry into SLI-aware buckets. 3) Deliver a production dashboard with drilldowns and suggested remediation (retry/scale/fallback) linked to runbooks. Scope: - Trace enrichment: add 3 trace hook attributes (failure_reason, model_variant, downstream_latency_ms) to span roots and request middleware. - Logging pipeline: add a transformation to annotate log entries with failure buckets at ingestion (using a mapping table in the metrics pipeline). - Metrics: expose histogram and count metrics per failure_bucket and per-model-variant. - Dashboard: build an interactive Failure Saga Explorer that correlates top traces, metric spikes, and sample logs; supports filtering by time, route, model, and capacity tier. Acceptance criteria: - Failure buckets (timeout, overload, model_error, transport_error, client_error, unknown) documented and represented in telemetry. - End-to-end enrichment validated on synthetic incidents (see test plan). - Dashboard supports click-to-open GitHub PR/Issue and Confluence runbook links. - Default SLI mapping and suggested alert thresholds included. Out of scope: automated remediation, UI overhaul of Console beyond the Explorer panel. Implementation notes: - Use tracehook v2 to attach failure_reason string to root spans; failure_reason must be one of the canonical buckets. - Add a lightweight enrichment transform in the log ingestion (Fluentd lambda) so logs get failure_bucket and trace_id. - Metrics pipeline (Prometheus/OTel exporter path) should emit failure_bucket_count{bucket="...", model="...", route="..."}. - Dashboard queries should include a deterministic scoring function that weights trace-level evidence (span error flags, HTTP/gRPC codes) and model-level signals (response length, token rejection rates). Rollout plan: feature flag to enable detailed failure enrichment per route; initial rollout to non-critical routes for 2 weeks; expand to high-traffic routes after validation. Risks & mitigations: - Increased cardinality (many model variants × routes) — mitigate by defaulting to top-k model variants and using label aggregation. - Perf impact of enrichment — keep tracehook work minimal (strings only), and add sampling for high-QPS routes. - False positives in bucket mapping — include human-in-the-loop feedback channel to correct mappings and update transform rules. Links: - Design/Spec: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/Failure+Saga+Explorer - Runbooks: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Failure+Playbooks - Incident replay dataset (GDrive): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1Example - Draft dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/obs/failure-saga-explorer
comments: 2026-03-10: Kickoff with Observability team. Aligned on canonical buckets and initial scope (trace enrichment + log transform + Grafana panel). Action: Marcus to prototype tracehook changes.
2026-03-11: Marcus pushed a spike PR for tracehook v2 attributes. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/tracehook/pull/142 — feedback from infra: ensure span size impact < 256 bytes.

2026-03-12: Design review with PM and SRE. Decision: use a scored evidence model for attribution rather than simplistic priority ordering. TODO: add unit tests for scoring function and provide accepted thresholds.

2026-03-12: Added log transform draft in staging fluentd pipeline. Test dataset ingestion shows failure_bucket tagging for 92% of synthetic incidents. Remaining 8% unknowns logged to failure-bucket-unclassified topic for manual review.

2026-03-13: Dashboard skeleton created in Grafana with three panels (Top failure buckets, Trace timeline with enriched spans, Sample logs with links). PR for dashboard json: https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability-dashboards/pull/78 — code review requested from @ElenaGarcia and @OmarR.
2026-03-13: Noted dependency on metric cardinality cap. Action: create migration plan to roll labels into aggregated_summary when variant count > 10.

2026-03-13: QA plan: run three synthetic incident scenarios (client timeout, overload via connection storm, model rejection spurious outputs) against staging pipeline and verify dashboard buckets and suggested remediation match expected mapping.
test_plan: 1) Unit tests for scoring function and bucket mapping (local). 2) End-to-end synthetic incident runs: create synthetic traces/logs for each bucket and validate enrichment, metric emission, and dashboard visualization. 3) Load test: enable enrichment on a copy of a high-QPS route in staging and measure CPU/memory and traceback payload sizes. 4) Oncall drill: trigger a controlled overload on low-traffic route and validate playbook steps and alerting. Success criteria: enriched traces for >95% synthetic incidents and <3% CPU regression on instrumentation path.
implementation_steps: - Spike: add failure_reason attribute to tracehook root span (Marcus). - Log transform: add failure_bucket annotation in Fluentd stage (SRE). - Metrics: add exporter for failure_bucket_count (Telemetry team). - Dashboard: build Grafana panels and scoring queries (Observability dev). - Testing: synth incidents and load test (QA & SRE). - Telemetry spike review, tune label cardinality (Infra). - Rollout behind feature flag then gradual ramp (Observability + SRE).
acceptance_criteria: - Canonical failure taxonomy implemented across traces/logs/metrics. - Grafana Failure Saga Explorer shows correlated traces, metrics, and logs with links to runbooks. - SLI mapping and default alert thresholds present in dashboard. - Performance overhead within agreed limits (<3% CPU on instrumented paths).
